title: Alternative Spellings for Known Sounds
keyIdea: One phoneme (sound) can be spelled by more than one grapheme (letter or letters). The j sound can be j, g, ge or dge (jam, giraffe, cage, bridge). The s sound can be s, c or ce (sun, city, mice). The n sound can be n, kn or gn (net, knot, gnome), and the r sound can be wr (write). Some spellings have a silent letter. Clues help you choose: c says s before e, i or y, and dge comes after a short vowel sound.

kid: You know lots of sounds. Now you will find new ways to write them. The j sound is j in jam. It is g in giraffe, ge in cage and dge in bridge.
Some letters hide. In knot you do not say the k. The k and the n go together and say n. In wrap, the w is quiet, so wr says r.
c can say two sounds. Look at the next letter. If it is e, i or y, c says s, like in city. If not, c says k, like in cat.
At the end of a word, the j sound is dge or ge. Say the vowel. A short sound, like the a in bad, takes dge: badge. A long sound, like the a in day, takes ge: cage.
adult: This is the Year 2 phonics step in the English National Curriculum: children learn alternative graphemes for phonemes they already know. It matches the US Common Core standards RF.1.3 and RF.2.3, which ask children to know spelling-sound correspondences and to decode words with common spelling patterns. A phoneme is a sound; a grapheme is the letter or letters that spell it.

The key correspondences here are /dʒ/ as j, g, ge and dge; /s/ as c and ce (soft c before e, i, y); /n/ as kn and gn; /r/ as wr; and /ʒ/ as s in treasure and television. In kn, gn and wr the first letter is silent, but it still belongs to the grapheme. The dge spelling follows a short vowel (badge, hedge, fudge), while ge follows a long vowel or a consonant (cage, huge, large).

Common mistakes: reading every c as k (saying kity for city), sounding the silent letter (k-nock), splitting kn or dge into separate sounds when counting phonemes, and using j at the end of a word (apart from a few borrowed words such as Raj, English words do not end in j). Children may also think a word with an unusual spelling is spelled wrong. Be careful to say the pure sound, not 'juh' or 'nuh'.

In the lab your child posts words into sound houses, taps every letter that makes a sound (including the silent ones), drags dge or ge onto a word by listening to its vowel, and uses the letter after c to choose between k and s.

familyTip: Go on a sound hunt in a book. Pick one sound, such as j, and write each word you find under its spelling: j, g, ge or dge. Ask: which spelling did we find most often? Which word has a quiet letter?

visual.caption: Which sound? Drag each word to its sound house, or tap it and then tap a house.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: post words into sound houses, find hidden letters, choose dge or ge, and read soft c.

practice.prompt: Which word has the n sound spelled kn?
practice.hint: Look for a k you cannot hear at the start.
practice.explain: In knee, the k is silent. kn says n. Nest and neck use the plain n spelling.

practice.prompt: Ravi finds {a} words with ge and {b} words with dge. All of them have the j sound. How many j words did he find?
practice.hint: ge and dge both spell the j sound. Add the two groups.
practice.explain: {a} and {b} make {=a+b} words. Two spellings, one sound: j.

practice.prompt: What sound does c make in “face”?
practice.hint: Look at the letter just after c.
practice.explain: c comes before e, so it says s. Face sounds like f-ai-s.

practice.prompt: A word starts with kn and has {n} letters. kn makes one sound, and every other letter makes its own sound. How many sounds?
practice.hint: k and n share one sound because the k is silent.
practice.explain: {n} letters, but k and n make one sound, so there are {=n-1} sounds. Knot: 4 letters, 3 sounds, n-o-t.

pool.prompt: Which word has the j sound spelled g?
pool.hint: Say each word. Which one starts with j but is spelled with g?
pool.explain: Giraffe starts with the j sound, spelled g. Jelly uses j, and goat has a hard g sound.

pool.hint: wr at the start of a word makes one sound.
pool.explain: wr says r, so write sounds just like right. The w is silent.

pool.prompt: Which ending finishes “bri_” to make bridge?
pool.hint: Is the i in bridge short or long?
pool.explain: The i in bridge is short, so the j sound is spelled dge.

pool.prompt: Which word has a soft c that says s?
pool.hint: c says s before e, i or y.
pool.explain: In city, c comes before i, so it says s. In cot and cup, c says k.

pool.prompt: Mo reads “knock” as k-nock. What should he change?
choices: Not say the k: kn says n
pool.hint: Which letter in knock makes no sound?
pool.explain: The k in knock is silent. kn says n, so it is n-o-ck.

pool.prompt: Which word has the zh sound, like the middle of television?
pool.hint: Say each word slowly. Listen for a soft buzzy sound.
pool.explain: In treasure, s says zh. Sun has the s sound and ship has sh.

pool.prompt: A sound house for s has {a} words with s, {b} words with c and {k} words with ce. How many words are in the house?
pool.hint: s, c and ce all spell the s sound. Add all three groups.
pool.explain: {a} + {b} + {k} = {=a+b+k} words, three spellings of one sound.

pool.prompt: Which ending finishes “ca_” to make cage?
pool.hint: Is the a in cage short like in bad, or long like in day?
pool.explain: The a in cage is long, so the j sound is spelled ge, not dge.

pool.prompt: Which word starts with gn, where the g is quiet?
pool.hint: Find the word that starts with the n sound.
pool.explain: In gnome, gn says n. Goat starts with a hard g and gem with a j sound.

pool.prompt: A word ends in dge and has {n} letters. d, g and e make one sound together. Every other letter makes its own sound. How many sounds?
pool.hint: Three letters, d g e, share one sound. Take away the two extra letters.
pool.explain: {n} letters, but dge is one sound, so there are {=n-2} sounds. Badge: 5 letters, 3 sounds, b-a-dge.
